evidence: ABSENCE: `apply_inbound_records` is never imported or referenced in the test module (search returned no matches), yet _field_contract.py module docstring cites it as a handled surface and the guard is said to cover 'the differ/apply path'

_field_contract.py:12-16: `Every reconciled field handled by the differ/apply path MUST have a :class:FieldSymmetry entry ... it fails collection when a field handled by conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES or inbound_differ._OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD lacks an entry`
docs/architecture.md:142-144: `a field handled by the conflict resolver or the differ's name-canonicalization map without a registry entry fails test collection`
advisory.finding: The coverage guard's documented contract is overstated: the docstrings, docs/architecture.md, and ticket AC claim it fails collection for any field 'handled by the differ/apply path' / 'apply_inbound_records', but the guard's only sources are conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES and inbound_differ._OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD. apply_inbound_records is never inspected, so an add-wins field handled only there (absent from FIELD_CLASSES) would not fail collection despite the stated guarantee.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either enforce parent's conflict_class against the real resolver behavior (or document that parent is intentionally not in FIELD_CLASSES and its conflict_class is unenforced), so the FieldSymmetry docstring's parity claim holds.
evidence: test_field_contract_properties.py:104-106 (parity): iterates `for name, cls in _conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES.items()` — parent, being absent, is never asserted
_field_contract.py FieldSymmetry docstring: `conflict_class ... must equal conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES[key] ... the parity test keeps the two from drifting`
advisory.finding: FieldSymmetry.conflict_class parity is not enforced for 'parent': parent is absent from conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES and the parity test iterates FIELD_CLASSES.items(), so parent's declared conflict_class='state' is never checked against any real source, contradicting the field's docstring ('must equal conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES[key]') and the anti-drift claim.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Parameterize the per-class property assertions off FIELD_CONTRACT `.symmetry` (iterate declared bidirectional/add_wins/one_way_gated entries) so every declared field — not just the four hardcoded ones — is exercised through the mechanism its class names.
evidence: test_core_field_classes_pinned pins `.symmetry` by literal field name only: `assert FIELD_CONTRACT["status"].symmetry == c.BIDIRECTIONAL` (test_field_contract_properties.py:116-120)

The behavioral status tests key off `.lossy_values`, not `.symmetry`: `lossy = FIELD_CONTRACT["status"].lossy_values` (test_field_contract_properties.py:131) — flipping status.symmetry leaves them green

The coverage guard asserts existence + conflict_class parity only, not per-class behavior: `missing = handled - declared` (test_field_contract_properties.py) and test_conflict_class_parity_with_field_classes (lines 105-110)

ABSENCE: no test iterates `[e for e in FIELD_CONTRACT.values() if e.symmetry == BIDIRECTIONAL]` (or ADD_WINS/ONE_WAY_GATED) to exercise each declared entry through its mechanism; ticket AC states 'Roundtrip identity asserted only for declared-bidirectional codecs' implying declaration-driven coverage
advisory.finding: The registry's declared `symmetry` class is never bound to the owning mechanism THROUGH the declaration: every per-class property test is hardcoded to literal field names (status/labels/links/parent) and keys off `.lossy_values`/`.removal_gate`/name, never iterating FIELD_CONTRACT by `.symmetry`. The import-time coverage guard only asserts an entry EXISTS and mirrors conflict_class. So a field declared `bidirectional` with a codec that does not round-trip (or an add_wins/one_way_gated field whose declared class is wrong) is undetectable for any field beyond the four hardcoded ones — the class the registry exists to enforce is not enforced generically.
scenarios: A new reconciled field is added, declared `bidirectional`, with a status/value codec that is silently non-injective — coverage guard passes (entry exists) and no round-trip test runs for it
An existing field's symmetry class is mis-declared (e.g. a set field declared bidirectional) for any field other than status/labels/links/parent
advisory.suggested_fix: Add declaration-driven tests: for each entry with symmetry==BIDIRECTIONAL that names a codec, assert round-trip on its canonical preimages; for each ONE_WAY_GATED entry, assert its named removal_gate is the real should_propagate_removal and is consulted; for each ADD_WINS entry, assert the add-wins property. Drive the loop off FIELD_CONTRACT.values() rather than literal field names.
